pins.agent_did_rule: The key named in verification_method is listed under capabilityDelegation in the issuer's DID document at issued_at (RFC-001 §6.2.1)

verification_options.trust_root: the root's issuer is the case's issuer DID
verification_options.signing_time_evidence: none: no case carries a timestamp or transparency-log entry for the signing time
verification_options.log_entries_known_at_now: every log entry is dated at or before now; run.mjs fails otherwise

cases.title: Delegation modified after signing (scope changed, delegation_id recomputed)
cases.note: The code is pinned so that another failure, such as ID_MISMATCH, cannot pass this case (#177, comment 6753745622). The signature is APS's check. Agent-DID's column only covers which key the DID authorizes, which the tampering does not change.

cases.title: Key retired before issued_at
cases.note: APS column corrected to KEY_AMBIGUOUS by the APS author in #177 (comment 6747421782): the claimed issued_at alone cannot place the signature before or after the retirement.

cases.title: DID deactivated after issued_at
cases.note: KEY_AMBIGUOUS is the APS author's reading of §3.4's general rule; the draft does not address DID deactivation explicitly (#177, comment 6747421782).

cases.title: Key never listed in the issuer's DID
cases.note: Added in #177 (comments 6751947600, 6752140683) so that KEY_NOT_FOUND stays exercised: the key never appears in the issuer's authoritative key history.

cases.title: Key added to the issuer's DID after issued_at
cases.note: Proposed after the APS author's review in #177 (comment 6753745622): the key appears in the issuer's log, but only from a version later than the claimed issued_at, and no retirement or deactivation is involved. Inputs come from generate-case-9.mjs.
